A.explanation: Far too small for a 60 cm metal sphere - $0.1 \text{ kg}$ is about the mass of an apple.

B.explanation: Too small by about a factor of 100 - a 60 cm copper sphere has volume about $0.1 \text{ m}^3$ and copper is much denser than water.

C.explanation: Volume about $0.1 \text{ m}^3$ times copper density about $9000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ gives about $1000 \text{ kg}$.

D.explanation: Far too large - $100000 \text{ kg}$ would need a volume about 100 times larger, so a diameter several times 60 cm.

hints: Start with the 60 cm diameter: convert to radius in metres, so $r = 0.30 \text{ m}$, ready for a volume in $\text{m}^3$.
Recall the sphere volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ and that $r^3 = 0.027 \text{ m}^3$, so $V$ is of order $0.1 \text{ m}^3$.
Connect mass to density with $m = \rho V$ and use $\rho \approx 9000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ for copper, much denser than water at $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
walkthrough: Identify the size in SI units: diameter $= 60 \text{ cm} = 0.60 \text{ m}$, so radius $r = 0.30 \text{ m}$.
State the volume rule for a sphere: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
Substitute the estimate: $r^3 = (0.30)^3 = 0.027 \text{ m}^3$, so $V \approx 4 \times 0.027 \approx 0.11 \text{ m}^3$, of order $0.1 \text{ m}^3$.
State the mass rule $m = \rho V$ and recall copper density $\rho \approx 9 \times 10^3 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Calculate: $m \approx 9000 \times 0.11 \approx 1000 \text{ kg}$ with unit $\text{kg}$, clearly far larger than 10 kg and far smaller than 100000 kg.
